```{r setup-network, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7, dpi = 110)
```

```{=html}
<hr>
<h1 id="network">Network: which associations survive conditioning?</h1>

<div class="block-box">
<strong>What a network estimates.</strong> Each variable is a node; an edge is
the association between two nodes <em>after conditioning on every other node in
the model</em>. That is the difference from the correlation screen above: a
correlation between two items can be produced entirely by a third, and an edge
survives only if the pair still covaries once the rest are held constant.
<br><br>
<strong>Mixed graphical model.</strong> Nodes are of different types here -
continuous sliders and categorical answers - so the model is fitted with
<code>mgm</code> (Haslbeck &amp; Waldorp, 2020), which estimates each node from
the others by regularised regression on the scale that node calls for.
Regularisation means small edges are set to exactly zero rather than shrunk,
so the graph is already a selection.
<br><br>
<strong>The ring around each node</strong> is its predictability (Haslbeck &amp;
Waldorp, 2018): how much of that node the rest of the network accounts for,
<em>R</em><sup>2</sup> for continuous nodes and normalised accuracy for
categorical ones. A node with a thin ring is one the network says little about.
<br><br>
<strong>Edge stability</strong> re-estimates the model on bootstrap samples and
counts how often each edge survives. The column to read is
<code>propLtZ</code>: the proportion of resamples in which the edge was set to
zero. A high value means the edge is not reliably there.
<br><br>
<strong>Which respondents.</strong> <code>mgm</code> rejects missing values, so
the model is fitted on complete cases. Every missing value here is a
&ldquo;Geen mening&rdquo; answer on a policy slider - a real response option,
not a skipped question - so this drops the respondents most ambivalent about
those substances.
</div>
```
```{=html}
<div class="block-box"><p><strong>Not configured for the main study.</strong>
The pilots' node list named the first pilot's variables one by one. The main
study replaced the belief items, asks own use per substance group and has a
different emotion question, so that list does not apply and no network is
estimated here.</p>
<p>Which nodes belong in a network is a substantive choice, so it needs its own
node list rather than an automatic translation.</p></div>
```
